name: NEO Heavyweight Championship
notes: The promotion's own top title, first awarded at its December 2000 year-end supercard (already served).
epitaph: New Era Old School Wrestling's top title. Steve Dumars won it at the promotion's year-end supercard in December 2000, retained it against Matthew Reason at Snowed In on 18 February 2001 and again at Storm Warning on 7 May 2001, and was still champion in the promotion's report of 26 June 2001.

name: NEO Pacific Championship
notes: The promotion's own second-tier title, crowned by a four-man tournament that ran across this record's own January-February 2001 shows.
epitaph: New Era Old School Wrestling's second-tier title, created through a four-man tournament across its January and February 2001 shows. Amuro Balsa won that tournament on 18 February 2001; Messiah held the title by 11 April; Matt Saunders beat Messiah at Storm Warning on 7 May 2001 and was still champion on 26 June.

name: NEO Skyweight Championship
notes: The promotion's own weight-restricted (under 215 lbs) title; already held when this record's own January 2001 preshow opens.
epitaph: New Era Old School Wrestling's title for wrestlers under 215 pounds. Sushi Tsunami held it when the promotion's January 2001 preshow opened, and Psicopa won it from Sushi Tsunami in a ladder match at Storm Warning on 7 May 2001, still champion on 26 June.

name: NEO Rocky Mountain Tag Team Championship
notes: The promotion's own tag title, first awarded in a four-way elimination match at Storm Warning, 7 May 2001.
epitaph: New Era Old School Wrestling's Rocky Mountain Tag Team Championship, first awarded to Monkey You in a four-way elimination match at Storm Warning on 7 May 2001. The new champions were attacked after the match by the Forces of Chaos and were still champions on 26 June 2001.

name: NEO Alberta Television Championship
notes: The promotion's own television title, long vacant before a royal rumble filled it at the Crimson Glory supercard in 2002; defended on every broadcast thereafter by its own rule.
epitaph: New Era Old School Wrestling's television title, defended on every episode of "The Show" by the promotion's own rule. It had been vacant for some time when a royal rumble at Crimson Glory crowned "Vicious" Vic Valiant in 2002; Valiant retained it against Red Dragon on 23 August and drew with Jayson Graham on 8 September, and Kristoff St. Livingstone took it from him on 24 October, still champion when the record ends.
